summary: Targeted evidence hunt, 4 independent rework designs from snuepi assets, judge panel scoring

evidence.summary: The pain is real and well documented at the builder level. Vapi, Retell, n8n and Skool forums have many first-person threads about agents booking the wrong date or timezone, booking in the past, double-booking, saying "you're booked" when the tool call failed, and quoting prices that are not in the knowledge base. Almost all of this is debugging help for builders, though. I found no first-person posts from agencies saying they lost a client over a wrong booking or an invented price. Agency churn content comes almost entirely from platform vendors (Trillet, myvoiceaiconnect), and they put churn down to "perception" and unclear ROI, not to wrong commitments. The usual community fixes are cheap prompt tricks: inject {{now}} with a timezone, read the date back to the caller, pass explicit ISO offsets. Vapi's own docs now say that confirmation should be enforced in the builder's service, not in the prompt. That points directly at a deterministic gate before booking or quoting, but it also means the platforms may add one. GoHighLevel's help docs claim double-booking prevention is built into its native Voice AI, and its Ideas board has a request for the AI to recognise existing appointments. That gives GHL users a native alternative. On price: agencies resell receptionists at roughly $297-$997 a month plus $1,000-$3,000 setup, and some UK/US Skool agencies charge £750-£3,000 a month. Raw platform cost is about $0.07-$0.15 a minute. The nearest paid tool is Cekura (QA testing), at pay-as-you-go $0.25 per test minute or $0.05 per monitored call, or $500 a month for its Startup plan. That suggests an agency would pay roughly $30-$500 a month for a reliability layer. Hamming already sells testing that checks "a booking is confirmed only after the tool call succeeds". I found no startup selling a runtime commitment or policy gate for Vapi/Retell/GHL, but evidence of willingness to pay for one is only indirect. Caveats: Reddit was blocked from search, and support.vapi.ai and canny.io could not be fetched. Every quote below is a search snippet, and most post dates could not be confirmed.

findings.claim: Vapi builders report agents booking with the wrong year or date even when the current time is correct. The suggested fix is to set the timezone field and inject the current time.
findings.quote: [snippet] assistant had the correct current time, but the booking request still used a 2024 timestamp

findings.claim: A timezone mismatch between the calendar tool (UTC) and the agent's reasoning (Eastern) made the agent report booked slots as free.
findings.quote: [snippet] the calendar tool returned UTC (Z) times while the agent reasoned in Eastern time, so it reported booked slots as free

findings.claim: A Vapi builder reports that the agent's checkAvailability flow double-books, even with the timezone set to New York and the current time injected. No confirmed fix is shown.
findings.quote: [snippet] The issue I'm running into is that the calendar is double booking dates.

findings.claim: The LLM resolves relative dates ('Monday', 'tomorrow') one to two days off. The community workaround is to read the date back to the caller before booking.
findings.quote: [snippet] Requests like "Monday" were often resolved one to two days off

findings.claim: Vapi agents tell callers an appointment is booked when the webhook failed or the slot was rejected. This is the false-confirmation failure.
findings.quote: [snippet] the call logs show that our webhook has failed ... and the appointment slot was rejected / it thinks it has successfully booked the appointment

findings.claim: Vapi's own docs say prompts cannot enforce confirmation and that builders must enforce it in their own service. This validates a deterministic gate, and also shows platform awareness that raises absorption risk.
findings.quote: [snippet] Prompts guide the model, but they don't enforce approval. If an action needs a stronger confirmation, enforce it in your service.

findings.claim: A Retell builder reports the agent quoting prices and durations without checking the knowledge base, producing hallucinated figures that look close to the real ones.
findings.quote: [snippet] Agent does not check KB for prices and duration, give hallucination close to real thing!

findings.claim: Vapi users report the assistant retrieving the wrong pricing information and hallucinating numbers after a knowledge-base dataset update.
findings.quote: [snippet] assistant hallucinates numbers after updating trieve dataset

findings.claim: Retell's community guide calls 'Time range is in the past' a common booking error, caused by the LLM not knowing the current time.
findings.quote: [snippet] a common error is "Time range is in the past," which it attributes to the LLM not understanding the current time

findings.claim: A Retell + Cal.com agent loops on check_availability and never calls book_appointment. Booking reliability failures persist in Retell's native integrations.
findings.quote: [snippet] Agent repeatedly calls check_availability_cal instead of book_appointment_cal

findings.claim: n8n builders' AI agents book the wrong day for relative dates and shift times because timestamps are sent without an offset. The advice is to take field selection away from the model.
findings.quote: [snippet] The agent gets confused and sometimes books on the wrong date. / The agent is choosing start, end, duration, and summary, which causes wrong dates
findings.who: n8n community users (dental clinic workflow, WhatsApp scheduler)

findings.claim: In Skool AI Automation Society, a builder says voice agents handle new bookings but struggle with reschedules and cancellations, and asks what production architecture others use (27 comments).
findings.quote: [snippet] struggles with rescheduling and cancellations ... whether built-in Google Calendar integrations fully support cancellation and rescheduling

findings.claim: In Skool, an n8n builder reports the AI agent ignoring the Google Calendar availability check. Another reports a Vapi + Make agent offering times already marked busy.
findings.quote: [snippet] AI Agent ignores Google Calendar availability check in n8n

findings.claim: On the GoHighLevel Ideas board, users ask that Conversation AI recognise existing appointments before suggesting new ones, and point to a separate 'prevent double booking' request.
findings.quote: [snippet] have conversational ai recognize existing appointments before suggesting new one ... the need to prevent double booking

findings.claim: GoHighLevel's help docs claim its native Voice AI already prevents double-booking with real-time calendar checks. For GHL-native builds, this is counter-evidence and an absorption risk.
findings.quote: [snippet] Double-Booking Prevention: Real-time calendar checks prevent overlapping appointments

findings.claim: A QA vendor notes that wrong-timezone bookings look like 'success' in booking-rate metrics until a patient complains weeks later, and that DST changes or prompt drift can break agents that used to work.
findings.quote: [snippet] a wrong-timezone booking can pass as a "success" in a 95% booking rate until the patient complains weeks later

findings.claim: Agency-platform vendors attribute most receptionist-client churn to perception and unclear ROI, not wrong commitments. This counter-evidence suggests wrong bookings are not the main stated churn driver.
findings.quote: [snippet] most agency owners find that 70–80% of their cancellations fall into perception churn

findings.claim: A vendor guide for agencies says the mistakes driving the most churn and support tickets are operational, and that clients who can see a booking dashboard cancel less. This supports a visibility or proof angle.
findings.quote: [snippet] clients who can see their booking dashboard are much less likely to cancel because the AI doesn't feel like a black box

findings.claim: A Skool member's shared voice-agent offer prices retainers at $497/mo (Foundation) and $997/mo (Growth, 'most popular').
findings.quote: [snippet] $497/month "Foundation" tier and a $997/month "Growth" tier

findings.claim: A Skool-based agency community prices UK/US voice receptionist retainers at £750-£3,000/month.
findings.quote: [snippet] prices its UK and US voice receptionist retainers at £750 to £3,000 per month

findings.claim: White-label MSP pricing anchors are much lower: retail AI receptionists cost $59-$99/mo and white-label partners price an agent at $75-$150/mo. This limits room for add-on fees at the low end.
findings.quote: [snippet] white-label partners price a single agent at $75 to $150 per month

findings.claim: The all-in platform cost per minute is roughly Vapi $0.105, Retell $0.110 and Bland $0.143 at 20k minutes. That leaves agencies a large margin under $500-$1,000 retainers.
findings.quote: [snippet] all-in cost at 20,000 minutes at Vapi $0.105, Retell $0.110, Bland $0.143

findings.claim: Cekura, the nearest paid reliability tool for agencies, charges $0.25 per voice test minute, $0.05 per monitored call, or $500/mo for its Startup plan. This is a price anchor for agency spend on reliability.
findings.quote: [snippet] $0.25 per voice testing minute, $0.05 per monitored call ... Startup plan ($500/month)

findings.claim: Hamming sells tool-call contract testing for Retell/Vapi agents, including a check that a booking is confirmed only after the tool call succeeds. This is offline testing, not a runtime gate.
findings.quote: [snippet] checks ... that a booking is confirmed only after the tool call succeeds

findings.claim: Builders hand-roll deterministic gates: in one Vapi + Make + Calendly build, the agent may confirm only when a booking token is present. Vapi forum answers on 'guardrail hooks' are vague and point to custom code. No dedicated runtime policy-layer product turned up.
findings.quote: [snippet] the scheduling tool returns an explicit availability contract, and the agent may confirm only when a booking token is present
findings.who: Vapi forum user + Reddit thread summarised by search

findings.claim: Documented liability precedent: a tribunal held Air Canada to a discount its chatbot described, and a UK shop's after-hours chatbot was talked into an 80% discount. Businesses end up honouring invented terms.
findings.quote: [snippet] the airline must follow through with the chatbot's promised discount
findings.who: Developer write-up of Moffatt v Air Canada

findings.claim: A UK small business's after-hours chatbot was talked into an 80% discount on an £8,000+ order. The customer threatened small claims and called the bot the company's legal representative. The owner cancelled and refunded, and no money was lost under the code. This is the clearest first-person SMB case: the business had no visible notice saying the bot cannot authorise discounts, and no clean record of what the bot was allowed to offer.
findings.quote: [snippet] shop's AI chat assistant was talked down from a 25% discount to 80%, and the customer then placed an order of £8,000+ ... the customer pasted the fabricated code into the free-text order comments
findings.who: Anonymous UK small business owner on r/LegalAdviceUK, via a write-up (Reddit snapshot: reddit.sentinel-team.org/posts/1qxc7x9)

findings.claim: In the same thread, practitioner advice was to cancel and refund in full. Under UK law, an obvious pricing mistake caused by a system error, plus contract formation at dispatch, protects the SMB. So the legal exposure for small, obvious errors may be lower than the Moffatt framing suggests.
findings.quote: [snippet] there is an obvious and substantial mistake in the price offered generated by a systems error ... a court is only ever going to award him his money back, as long as you're giving him a FULL refund

findings.claim: BMW Toronto's AI chatbot 'Quinn' offered C$27,162.79 for a trade-in without saying it was an AI. The dealer withdrew the offer, then honoured it once CBC asked questions. The cost was roughly C$5-7k. A lawyer told CBC an agreement could be in place because the bot had moved to schedule a meeting. The dealer now has humans make final offers. The trigger was reputational, not legal.
findings.quote: [snippet] Sales manager Scott Shadbolt said the original chatbot offer of $27,162.79 would be honored to 'do right' by Giacomelli ... final numbers will come from humans only, and customers will be clearly told when they are talking to a chatbot
findings.who: BMW Toronto (dealer), customer Zack Giacomelli, CBC reporting via Carscoops

findings.claim: Priceline's 'Penny' chatbot promised a refund on a non-refundable booking. The company honoured the invented promise only once a national newspaper was watching. This shows a pattern: companies honour bot promises under media pressure, not by default.
findings.quote: [snippet] Priceline's "Penny" chatbot promised a refund on a non-refundable booking, then nobody wanted to pay it

findings.claim: Germany's OLG Hamm ruled (12 May 2026, Az. 4 UKl 3/25) that a website chatbot is part of the business. Its false statements, here invented specialist titles for doctors, are the operator's own commercial acts under the UWG (unfair competition law). Neither a disclaimer nor the involvement of an IT contractor protected the operator. An appeal to the BGH (Federal Court of Justice) is allowed. Reported as the first German higher-court ruling on this, and it is a strong EU signal.
findings.quote: [snippet] Der KI-Chatbot ist rechtlich Teil der geschäftlichen Organisation des Unternehmens ... Ein KI-Chatbot vergab großzügig nicht existierende Facharztbezeichnungen. Das OLG Hamm rechnet die Aussagen den verantwortlichen Ärzten zu – die Revision zum Bundesgerichtshof ist zugelassen.
findings.who: Legal Tribune Online (LTO), reporting on the OLG Hamm ruling

findings.claim: German chambers of commerce (IHK) and SME legal portals now warn that operators are liable for their chatbots and can receive Abmahnungen (cease-and-desist letters). That gives German SMBs a concrete, recurring exposure: competitors or associations can send warning letters over chatbot statements.
findings.quote: [snippet] Betreiber haften für ihren Chatbot
findings.who: IHK Chemnitz (chamber of commerce guidance for SMEs)

findings.claim: A Chinese court went the other way. The Hangzhou Internet Court refused to enforce a chatbot's promise of 100,000 yuan because AI lacks legal capacity to express intent, and the platform was protected where it showed reasonable safeguards. Case law is split, and showing safeguards was a defence.
findings.quote: [snippet] Artificial intelligence lacks the capacity for civil rights and therefore cannot make legally recognized expressions of intent
findings.who: Shanghai Daily, reporting a Hangzhou Internet Court ruling

findings.claim: In the US, Smith v. Substack held that a customer-service chatbot's responses were not definite enough to support promissory estoppel (enforcing a promise someone relied on). Vague bot statements may not bind; specific prices and offers are the real risk.
findings.quote: [snippet] a customer service chatbot's responses were not sufficiently definite to give rise to a claim of promissory estoppel

findings.claim: Cursor's AI email-support bot 'Sam' invented a login policy that did not exist. It caused visible subscription cancellations after HN and Reddit threads, and the co-founder apologised on HN. HN commenters were angry that the bot was not labelled as AI. A developer-tool company lost revenue from one invented policy statement.
findings.quote: [snippet] this is an incorrect response from a front-line AI support bot ... not labelled as such is clearly intended to be deceptive
findings.who: Cursor rep on Reddit; HN commenters; co-founder Michael Truell

findings.claim: A Reddit user said a Verizon chat agent offered a free iPhone 17 Pro Max with no trade-in, and a later agent called the offer invalid. Verizon honoured it after escalation. The user's evidence was chat transcripts and screenshots. Caveat: the agent may have been human, not AI. It is still relevant to the 'proof of what was said' need: consumers already rely on transcripts as evidence.
findings.quote: [snippet] a chat agent offered a free iPhone 17 Pro Max with no trade-in, a supervisor allegedly approved it, and a later agent called it invalid ... phone reps can't see promotions offered through chat

findings.claim: A small-business blogger testing AI receptionists found the bot quoted a specific boiler-service price (£89) that was not his real rate. Practitioners advise routing all pricing and negotiation to a human. This is first-person evidence that SMB voice agents invent prices.
findings.quote: [snippet] it gave a specific figure, £89, that wasn't his price at all ... anything mentioning a complaint, an emergency, or a price negotiation goes to a human, full stop
findings.who: Lilach Bullock (SMB blogger testing AI receptionists)

findings.claim: Voice-AI vendors and QA firms now openly treat invented discounts as a margin and contract-dispute risk. SignalWire argues that prompt rules make it worse and that the model must not handle price data at all. This supports a deterministic 'commitment firewall' approach, but it also means platforms are starting to build the same thing themselves.
findings.quote: [snippet] if you tell the model "don't mention the discount," you have now increased the probability that it will

findings.claim: In a QA case study for a dental client, Retell's QA tool found a 12% hallucination rate on certain patient questions. Hamming, Haptik and Retell all sell or publish hallucination detection for voice agents, so offline QA is already a crowded competitor category.
findings.quote: [snippet] ungrounded AI agents can improvise commitments such as unapproved discount rates, extended payment deadlines, or waived penalties

findings.claim: Armilla (a Lloyd's coverholder, backed by Chaucer) raised its standalone AI liability limits to $25M. Cover now includes harmful or misleading outputs, wrong decisions, improper tool use and escalation errors. Payouts are performance-triggered (accuracy falling below a baseline, for example from 95% to 85%), and underwriters refuse systems they judge too error-prone. That means insurers need measured performance data and evidence. No prices are published.
findings.quote: [snippet] coverage would only be activated if the insurer determines that the AI tool's performance fell below initial expectations

findings.claim: Testudo (a Lloyd's coverholder that insures companies deploying AI, not building it) expanded capacity with Atrium and QBE to $9.25M. It cites generative-AI litigation up 137% year on year. It will not underwrite AI vendors or firms that customise foundation models.
findings.quote: [snippet] Testudo's policy is designed to respond to third-party claims arising from AI-generated outputs, covering legal costs and damages where conventional commercial general liability insurance may not apply

findings.claim: Munich Re's HSB launched AI liability cover for businesses with 1-500 employees on 18 March 2026. It is sold only as an add-on through partner carriers' business policies and covers bodily injury, property damage and advertising injury. It does not appear to cover promised refunds or discounts, which are contractual or economic loss. HSB's survey: 74% of SMBs use AI and 91% plan to.
findings.quote: [snippet] HSB does not offer this product directly to businesses ... Business sizes include microbusinesses (1-10 employees), small businesses (11-50 employees), and medium businesses (51-500 employees)

findings.claim: Munich Re's aiSure, through Mosaic, now offers up to €15M of parametric cover (pays out on a defined trigger) for AI performance failures. The threshold is defined per risk, written into the policy and checked against real-world outcomes. That creates demand for independent, verifiable performance and interaction logs.
findings.quote: [snippet] It is defined individually for each risk, based on the specific AI model and the guarantee the insured has issued to their customer
findings.who: Mosaic Insurance head of AI underwriting / Munich Re aiSure

findings.claim: From January 2026, ISO (Verisk) optional generative-AI exclusions (CG 40 47 / 40 48 / 35 08) are available for general liability policies, and their 'arising out of' wording is broad. Separately, a guide notes that refunds or promises a chatbot makes are usually treated as the business's own cost and are not insurable. So the honour-the-promise loss is generally uninsured: the cost falls on the SMB.
findings.quote: [snippet] refunds or promises a chatbot makes are usually treated as the business's own cost, not an insurable loss. Most liability policies don't pay for them.

findings.claim: The revised EU Product Liability Directive (2024/2853) treats software and AI systems as products under strict liability, with a transposition deadline of 9 December 2026. Courts can order disclosure of technical records. It mainly hits AI providers rather than deploying SMBs, and covers harm such as data loss rather than promised discounts.
findings.quote: [snippet] 'product' to specifically include electricity, digital manufacturing files and software, including operating systems, firmware, computer programs, applications and AI systems

findings.claim: The EU's planned Digital Fairness Act explicitly covers chatbots used for customer service, including AI chatbots as the only way to contact a business, alongside personalised and dynamic pricing. It is still a proposal; its content and date are unconfirmed as of these sources.
findings.quote: [snippet] AI chatbots when used as sole means of communication with customers

findings.claim: Lawyers advise that AI conversation logs are discoverable evidence (ESI under FRCP 34, the US federal discovery rule). Defence reviews scrutinise log authenticity, chain of custody, account identity and deletion policy. Engineering writers recommend immutable audit logs kept separate from content, which matches a signed, hash-chained record. The material is mostly law-firm and vendor commentary, with no first-person SMB buyer asking for it.
findings.quote: [snippet] authenticity of logs, chain of custody, user account identity, login records, deletion/back-up policy, context of use
findings.who: Tian Pan (engineering blog); law firms Katten, Blakes

findings.claim: In the Delaware case Fortis Advisors v. Krafton (March 2026), a CEO's chatbot logs were used as evidence of intent in a $250M earnout dispute. AI transcripts are already decisive evidence in high-value disputes, though for enterprises, not SMBs.
findings.quote: [snippet] a court treated the CEO's lengthy AI chat logs as evidence of the defendant's strategic intent — and bad faith

findings.claim: Commentators recommend contractual limits and visible terms, such as 'this bot cannot make offers or authorise discounts', as the main mitigation. Air Canada failed partly because the correct policy sat on a different page and was not tied to the conversation. That supports showing the binding terms inside the conversation and keeping a record of them, which is close to what snuepi's terms snapshot does.
findings.quote: [snippet] Air Canada does not appear to have relied on website terms that might have disclaimed liability

evidence.summary: Pain is real and keeps recurring, but it is mostly a reputational loss that SMBs absorb rather than a liability they would pay to prove. In 2026 there were several first-person or reported cases: a UK SMB's chatbot gave an 80% discount on an £8k order, BMW Toronto was out roughly C$5-7k, Priceline's Penny invented a refund, Verizon chat promises were disputed, and an AI receptionist invented an £89 price. In most of them the business either honoured the promise under media pressure or used an obvious-mistake defence. Law is moving toward holding the operator liable, especially in the EU: OLG Hamm (May 2026) attributes chatbot statements to the business regardless of disclaimers, and German IHKs now warn SMEs about warning letters (Abmahnungen). Other courts went the other way: a Hangzhou court refused enforcement and US Smith v. Substack required definite promises. Insurers are entering: Armilla up to $25M, Testudo $9.25M, HSB SMB add-ons sold through carriers, and Munich Re aiSure/Mosaic €15M parametric cover. The promised-discount loss itself is generally uninsurable, and ISO AI exclusions from January 2026 widen the gap. Insurers' performance-triggered and parametric policies need measured, verifiable records, which may make insurers and MGAs (managing general agents) a better buyer for signed AI-interaction evidence than SMBs themselves. No public premiums or SMB budgets surfaced; willingness to pay is inferred only from insurer capacity and litigation growth (Testudo reports +137% year on year). Competition on prevention is crowded (Hamming, Retell QA, Haptik, SignalWire's own guidance against passing price data to the model), so the defensible angle is deterministic commitment control plus a court- and insurer-grade record of what the agent offered and under which terms. Evidence quality caveat: nearly all of this is search snippets and secondary write-ups; the Reddit threads were seen only through snapshot mirrors.

I ran 20 searches and found no verified production case of a merchant or PSP losing, or even fighting, a chargeback on an agent-placed purchase. There are no first-person merchant, PSP or dispute-analyst posts on Reddit, HN or Shopify Community either. Nearly everything comes from chargeback vendors (Chargebacks911, Justt, Chargeflow, Chargeback Gurus, chargeback.io) and aggregator blogs (stellagent, tinyfish Current), and they argue from scenarios rather than case counts. Three real production incidents turned up, all next to the dispute question rather than inside it. (1) Fowler, Feb 2025: OpenAI's Operator bought eggs on Instacart without being asked. No chargeback was reported. (2) Amazon "Buy for Me", Dec 2025 to Jan 2026: brands were enrolled without consent and fulfilled orders without knowing Amazon placed them. Only a secondhand Reddit warning links this to chargebacks. (3) ChatGPT Instant Checkout reached only a handful of merchants and was scaled back around March 2026 because people didn't buy through it, so the big agent checkout channel produced almost no volume to dispute. Industry players treat the risk as real, with protection products but no measured loss data. Amex Agent Purchase Protection (Apr 2026, cardholder-side, final terms not published) and Chargebacks911's merchant indemnity (27 Oct 2026, price and terms not public) both exist. Worldpay, Checkout.com and the vendors all say network dispute rules for agent transactions are unwritten. Merchant of record keeps the liability under ACP and Stripe SPT, and no agent-specific reason codes exist. Prices for dispute work today are mostly a share of what's won back: Chargeflow 25% of recovered plus $29 per deflected alert, Disputifier 20% capped at $250 per win, Justt and Chargebacks911 custom quotes. That signals budget is paid per recovered dispute, not for evidence infrastructure. The question also falls inside a lane where the incumbents are moving: Chargebacks911 already sells indemnity and a permission-trail record, and Visa is shipping AI dispute tools. A solo founder's standalone "agent dispute pack" would sit inside incumbents' roadmaps with no observed losses yet. For a rework, this evidence points away from the dispute pack and toward pain that is visible now: wrong bookings and commitments by agents (the TRUE GAP 26.8 theme), or consent and attribution evidence sold through an existing dispute vendor rather than straight to SMBs.

findings.claim: A real production incident: OpenAI Operator bought eggs on Instacart that the user had only asked it to find, and misreported the total. OpenAI blamed a failed confirmation step. No chargeback or merchant dispute was reported.
findings.quote: OpenAI's Operator agent spent a columnist's money on $31.43 of eggs he had asked it to find [snippet, title]; Operator reported the final tally as $19.68 [snippet, secondary summary]
findings.who: Geoffrey A. Fowler (Washington Post), via AI Incident Database / vibegraveyard summary

findings.claim: Amazon Buy for Me sent real agent-placed orders to small merchants who never opted in. One merchant fulfilled about 16 orders before realizing Amazon placed them. This is production pain, but a chargeback link is only claimed in a secondhand Reddit warning.
findings.quote: four other merchants who spoke to Modern Retail for this story were also upset that their products were featured on Amazon.com without their permission [snippet]
findings.who: Modern Retail reporting on SMB brand owners

findings.claim: A Reddit post (cited secondhand) warned Shopify sellers that Buy for Me may raise chargebacks. This was a warning, not a reported loss.
findings.quote: Buy For Me may result in an increase in credit card chargebacks [snippet, paraphrase of Reddit post cited by Value Added Resource]
findings.who: Anonymous Reddit seller, cited by Value Added Resource

findings.claim: ChatGPT Instant Checkout, the main agent checkout channel, reached only a handful of merchants and was scaled back around March 2026 because users researched there but didn't buy, so there was almost no transaction volume to dispute.
findings.quote: Instant Checkout had been pulled back due to "lackluster performance," and only a handful of merchants ever went live with it [snippet, Forrester cited]

findings.claim: Chargebacks911 launched merchant-side indemnity against qualifying chargebacks on AI-agent purchases. It is sold as a bolt-on that doesn't replace existing fraud tools. Pricing and coverage limits weren't published.
findings.quote: identifies transactions involving AI agents and provides indemnification against qualifying chargebacks associated with those purchases [snippet]
findings.who: Chargebacks911 (vendor press release via The Paypers)

findings.claim: Chargebacks911's framing of the problem ('I didn't buy that, my AI did'): disputes arise even when the agent did exactly what it was told. This is a scenario-based warning, not case data.
findings.quote: The card wasn't stolen, the merchant made no error, and the agent operated within its settings. Yet disputes still occur [snippet]

findings.claim: Chargebacks911 already sells a record of the permission trail as part of its dispute platform. This overlaps directly with a 'dispute pack' built from consent and evidence data.
findings.quote: Unified Dispute Management System records permission trails, transaction activity and timestamped actions across the payment process [snippet, paraphrase]

findings.claim: Amex Agent Purchase Protection covers cardholders for errors by a registered agent. It applies only to US Amex cards, only to agents built on Amex's developer kit, and only after the cardholder tries a return. Full terms are 'to come'. It is written for cardholders, not merchants.
findings.quote: available for eligible charges only after the Card Member has initiated a return (where possible) with the merchant [snippet]
findings.who: American Express (network) via Fortune / Amex agentic-commerce page

findings.claim: Worldpay (an acquirer) says who bears the loss on agent disputes beyond plain fraud is still undecided, even though all three networks have launched agent frameworks.
findings.quote: liability allocation between merchant, issuer and agent platform remains largely unresolved once a dispute moves past straightforward fraud [snippet, paraphrase]

findings.claim: Mastercard publicly says its standard chargeback protections apply to agent-completed transactions. There is no agent-specific rule or reason code.
findings.quote: Mastercard said its standard chargeback protections apply if users dispute a transaction completed by an AI agent [snippet, paraphrase of BankInfoSecurity]

findings.claim: Under Stripe's agentic commerce stack (ACP/SPT), the merchant stays merchant of record and keeps control of refunds and disputes. Stripe publishes no special agent-dispute split.
findings.quote: As the merchant of record, you also retain all control over customer relationships, including how refunds and disputes are managed. [snippet]

findings.claim: Justt (a dispute vendor) says merchants carry full dispute liability under ACP.
findings.quote: Under ACP, the merchant remains the MOR. You retain control over payment processing and you bear full liability for disputes. [snippet]

findings.claim: Chargeback vendors say no agent-specific reason code exists, and that a dispute defense needs proof of consent for each order (the delegation, the approved cart, the agent's identity). This is the same evidence the planned dispute pack would assemble, and vendors are already writing playbooks for it.
findings.quote: agent disputes use the existing Visa and Mastercard reason codes, and no agent-specific code exists yet [snippet, paraphrase]

findings.claim: Chargeflow has published an 'evidence playbook' for agentic chargebacks and says merchants pay by default because no rule assigns fault.
findings.quote: No framework for AI-initiated authorization or disputes exists under Regulation E [snippet]

findings.claim: Visa shipped general (not agent-specific) AI dispute tools in April 2026 (Dispute Intelligence, Doc Analyzer), with its Dispute Resolution Network planned for general availability in late 2026. The network itself is moving into dispute automation.
findings.quote: Visa announced six AI-powered dispute tools [snippet, paraphrase]

findings.claim: An essay written from a dispute analyst's point of view says the hard case is a vague instruction, not fraud: a specific mandate gives usable evidence, while 'find me something good' does not. This is a thought piece, not a case log.
findings.quote: "you can't adjudicate a vibe" [snippet, title]

evidence.summary: The pain is real and it repeats. Builders on Vapi, GHL and Make post the same failures over and over: past or wrong dates, wrong time zones, double-booking because the create-event tool does not check for conflicts, and agents saying "you're booked" when the booking failed. The fix practitioners keep landing on is a deterministic gate in their own code (only confirm if a booking token exists). The platforms only partly absorb this. Vapi has tool rejection plans (Aug 2025), but its own docs say confirmation has to be enforced in your own service. Retell shipped content guardrails (Feb 2026), current-time variables per time zone (Mar 2026) and a duplicate-booking-call fix (Aug 2026). Native GHL and Synthflow show no booking-specific validation, and Synthflow now sells enterprise-only from about $30k/yr. Offline QA is funded and crowded: Coval raised a $28M Series A (Jun 2026, Norwest), Hamming about $3.8-4.3M seed, Cekura $2.4M seed with public prices ($0.25 per test minute, $500/mo startup plan). That gives a real price anchor for agency budgets. Runtime action guardrails are funded only as enterprise security (Capsule $7M, Asymptote $5.5M, Kontext $4M, CodeIntegrity about $5M), not as business-rule or commitment checks for SMB voice agents. That is the whitespace. AI liability insurance now exists and is tied to certification and audit evidence: AIUC $40M Series A (Sep 2026), whose AIUC-1-backed policy ElevenLabs was first to carry (Feb 2026); Armilla offers Lloyd's-backed limits up to $25M. Signed or hash-chained agent receipts are commoditizing: open-source Signet and ActionProof, plus an IETF draft from Aug 2026. Counter-evidence: (1) builders say they can fix this with a token gate in their own code; (2) Retell and Vapi keep shipping fixes; (3) the liability cases (BMW Toronto, Priceline, Air Canada) were settled by publicity at large firms, not SMBs; (4) I found no first-person post showing an agency paying for a runtime guard; (5) agency retainers ($1-3k/mo per client) leave room, but WTP for a separate guard is unproven.

designs.name: BookedRight: a commitment gate and client proof report for voice-agent agencies (snuepi rework)
designs.one_liner: One drop-in tool for Vapi, Retell, GHL and n8n agents that only lets the agent say "you're booked" or quote a price after snuepi has checked it against the client's real calendar and price list. Each week it also gives the agency a white-label, signed report of every booking and quote, which the agency forwards to its client to show the AI is working.

They charge $297-$997 a month per client (UK agencies £750-£3,000) plus setup. Start with English-speaking agencies in the UK, Ireland, the Nordics, DACH and the Benelux, then the US. A second buyer comes later: the white-label voice platforms these agencies sit on (Trillet, MyVoiceAIConnect, RingLogix-type MSP resellers).

designs.problem_evidence:
The pain is evidenced but not yet proven to drive churn. Strongest signals:
(1) Builders keep hitting the same commitment failures. Agents book with the wrong year (Vapi community m/1379750706482909185). UTC vs local time makes booked slots look free (support.vapi.ai 33208523). Double-booking (vapi community m/1376589305715359877; support.vapi.ai 29168749: the create-event tool has no conflict check). "Monday" resolves one to two days off (m/1375475162551554108). The agent says "booked" when the webhook failed (support.vapi.ai 27162858). Retell agents loop on check_availability (community.retellai.com 3496) and quote hallucinated prices (community.retellai.com 3393). n8n agents book wrong dates (community.n8n.io 259554). A Skool AI Automation Society builder asks what production architecture handles reschedules (27 comments).
(2) Platforms say the fix belongs outside the model. Vapi docs: "Prompts guide the model, but they don't enforce approval... enforce it in your service." Builders hand-roll a booking_token gate (Reddit snapshot 1tfc3ps). AInora: "Nothing outside the model checked the booking against the rule."
(3) The failures are invisible and drive churn through how clients perceive the AI. Roark: a wrong-timezone booking "can pass as a success... until the patient complains weeks later". Trillet: 70-80% of agency cancellations are "perception churn". MyVoiceAIConnect (2026-11-08): clients who can see a booking dashboard cancel less because the AI "doesn't feel like a black box". This is why the product sells proof to the agency's client, not only prevention.
(4) Price anchors: Cekura charges $500/mo (Startup) or $0.05 per monitored call. Agency guides price management at $1-3k per client per month or a $300-500 add-on, and suggest roughly $50-300 per client for a guard. Platform cost of about $0.10/min leaves margin.
(5) Invented prices on SMB lines are real: an AI receptionist quoted £89 for a boiler service (Lilach Bullock), a UK shop's chatbot gave an 80% discount on an £8k order, and BMW Toronto lost about C$5-7k.
What is missing: no first-person post from an agency saying it lost a client over a wrong booking, and no proof yet of willingness to pay for a runtime guard. The 25 calls must close that gap.
designs.product:
v1 is deliberately narrow. Booking plus price commitments, voice first, three integration paths.

1. Commitment tool (runtime gate). Vapi custom tools, a Retell custom function, a GHL Voice AI/workflow webhook and an n8n node all call the same small API:
- resolve_slot: takes natural-language date and time plus the client's time zone and today's date. It rejects past dates and weekday/date mismatches, is DST-safe, and returns a normalized slot plus a read-back sentence.
- check_and_hold: atomic free/busy plus a hold, against Google, Microsoft or Cal.com/Calendly/Acuity/Square/SimplyBook.
- commit_booking: writes the event and returns a commitment_id only when the write succeeded.
- quote: returns only prices and discounts from the client's price sheet (CSV or website import) within a max-discount rule, otherwise "a human will confirm".
The LLM never computes dates or prices. A drop-in prompt snippet plus a tool rejection plan forbids confirmation without a commitment_id.

2. Post-call reconciliation. An end-of-call webhook ingests the transcript. An LLM-plus-rules pass finds every claimed booking or price and checks it against the commitment log and calendar. Mismatches (said booked but no event, wrong time, price not on the sheet, invented discount) trigger a same-day alert to the agency (Slack or email).

3. Weekly proof report (white-label). A per-client page or PDF in the agency's branding: calls handled, bookings made and verified in the calendar, quotes given and matched to the price sheet, issues caught, revenue booked. Each line is backed by snuepi's signed, hash-chained record, so "the AI booked it, here is the proof" holds up in a client dispute.

4. Free "Booking Stress Test" (the sales hook). Snuepi's hostile-agent simulator places about 50 adversarial calls or chats against an agency's live agent: relative dates, DST week, double-booking attempts, discount haggling, failed-webhook scenarios. It returns a scored failure report.

Out of v1: payments and deposits, own phone numbers, chat widget, identity, multi-language beyond EN plus one, insurer exports.
designs.distribution:
Founder-led, inside the communities where agencies already gather and complain:
- Skool groups (AI Automation Society, voice-agency communities such as Pickup, offer-sharing groups), the Vapi and Retell Discords and forums, the n8n community and the GHL Facebook groups.
- Tactic: answer the exact threads cited above with a working fix plus "free stress test of your agent", then convert stress-test results into pilots. Use the existing snuepi-signals collector, retargeted at those forums, to surface fresh "agent booked wrong" threads daily.
- Within 2 months: list in the Vapi and Retell tool/template galleries and publish an n8n community node plus a GHL marketplace webhook app (low-effort listings).
- Within 6 months: partner with one or two white-label agency platforms and voice-QA-adjacent educators (Skool course owners take an affiliate cut of 20-30% recurring).
- The proof report itself spreads the product. Every end client sees "verified by snuepi" in small print, and agencies show it in sales calls as a reliability guarantee.
designs.pricing:
Priced per client agent, sized to fit inside a $500-1,000 agency retainer and below Cekura's $500 plan:
- Starter: $49 per client agent per month (gate plus reconciliation, up to 500 calls).
- Agency: $299/mo for up to 8 client agents, then $35 each, including the white-label proof report.
- Overage: $0.03 per reconciled call above caps.
- Paid pilot, the Gate B target: €750 (about $800) for 60 days, covering up to 5 client agents, done-with-you setup and stress tests on all 5. The fee is credited against the first 3 months if they convert, with a signed one-page order form and a card on file through Stripe.
Agencies are expected to resell this as a "no-double-booking, no-rogue-price guarantee" line item at $100-200 per client, which is the margin story for the buyer.
designs.moat:
Honest assessment: medium, and it compounds slowly.
Why platforms do not fully absorb it:
(a) Agencies are multi-platform: Vapi, Retell, GHL and n8n on different clients. One neutral layer with one client rule sheet beats four native partial fixes. Retell fixes slices (time variables, duplicate calls) and Vapi explicitly pushes enforcement to "your service".
(b) The hard part is SMB-specific: price lists, discount authority, services, durations, buffers, opening hours, holidays, and write-safe connectors to SMB booking systems (Acuity, Square, SimplyBook, Cal.com and others). Voice platforms do not want to own SMB business rules and booking-system integrations; that is where snuepi already has 20 connectors and a terms layer.
(c) The proof report sits in the agency-to-client relationship. Once an agency's clients receive it weekly, ripping it out is visible, which creates retention lock-in that has nothing to do with the gate.

What compounds:
- A cross-agency corpus of failure modes and stress-test scenarios that improves the gate and the free test.
- A per-client terms and price sheet that becomes the system of record for "what the AI may promise".
- The signed commitment history, which later becomes insurer-grade evidence (Armilla, Testudo and AIUC require measured performance; parametric cover needs verifiable logs).

Real threats:
- GHL claims native double-booking prevention, so GHL-only shops are a weaker segment.
- A strong builder can hand-roll a booking_token gate.
- Cekura or Hamming could add a runtime mode.
The defence is speed into agencies plus the reporting and price layer, not the date resolver alone.
designs.snuepi_reuse:
Roughly 65-75% of v1 already exists.
- Booking engine: free-time lookup, holds, confirm, cancel/move, opening hours, holidays and DST-safe time zones. This becomes resolve_slot, check_and_hold and commit_booking.
- Reply guard and post-guard: the logic that strips false "you're booked", promised discounts and outside links, repurposed into transcript reconciliation rules.
- Terms layer: price floors, deterministic negotiation and discount rules and the 9 sector defaults. Becomes the client price and discount sheet.
- One-approval activation: website reading of services, prices, hours and booking system, for 10-minute client onboarding.
- Calendar and booking connectors: Google, Microsoft, iCal, Cal.com, Calendly, Acuity, Square, SimplyBook, Setmore. All are tested only against imitations, so they must be validated live first. Hourly polling must be replaced by a live free/busy check at hold time.
- Signed hash-chained record and per-booking evidence bundle. Backs the proof report.
- Hostile-agent simulator and booking simulation, repurposed as the free Booking Stress Test.
- The MCP server and REST/OpenAPI collapse to about 6 endpoints.
- snuepi-signals, retargeted to agency forums.
- Fly/SQLite/Litestream infra and the EU LLM.
New code needed: Vapi/Retell/GHL/n8n adapters and tool templates, the transcript-ingest webhook, the white-label report and an agency multi-client dashboard (thin), plus 2FA and roles. Estimate 3-5k LOC.
designs.retire:
Drop the planned chargeback dispute-pack pivot. The evidence shows no observed agent-dispute losses, budgets paid per recovered dispute, and Chargebacks911, Chargeflow and Visa already in the lane.

Retire or freeze:
- Agent payments: ACP, UCP, Stripe shared payment tokens, AP2 mandates, OAuth customer mandates and spend limits.
- A2A and the per-business agent cards.
- Identity: Web Bot Auth verification, fake-brand detection, KYA/KYB, trust levels, outside identity tokens and the fraud score.
- Own phone doors (Twilio, Telnyx, SignalWire, Azure speech). Agencies bring Vapi or Retell.
- The email door, public booking page and website widget.
- Deposits, no-show fees and Stripe Connect (park for v2).
- The goods catalogue/ERP, buy, B2B quotes, case and consultation flows.
- Phrase-matching guardrails for regulated work, which over-refuse.
- The 48-business world simulator, the free terms registry and the "Agent Terms v1" standard push (keep the schema internally).
- Restaurant connectors (resOS, Formitable, TheFork, OpenTable) and the partner-gated Phorest, Mindbody and Vagaro (revisit on demand).
- 10 of the 12 languages.
- Norway leftovers.
Target: cut 444 routes to fewer than 40.
designs.validation_plan:
This is sell-first and stays inside the current gates. The only build before Gate B is a 1-week demo harness: one Vapi assistant and one Retell agent wired to the existing engine through custom tools, plus the stress-test runner pointed at an external agent's phone number or web call. That is a demo, not the product.

Weeks 1-4 (to 8 Dec, Gate A: 25 calls):
- Build a list of 120 agencies from Skool member posts, Vapi and Retell community answerers, n8n "AI receptionist" workflow sellers, and LinkedIn "AI voice agency" in the UK, Ireland, DACH, the Nordics and the Netherlands.
- Daily: reply helpfully to 3-5 live "agent booked wrong / said booked when it wasn't / invented price" threads with the fix and an offer of a free stress test.
- DM and email at 10-15 a day: "I'll run 50 adversarial booking calls against one of your client agents and send you the failure report, free, 48h."
- Each call follows a fixed script:
  (1) Last 90 days: any wrong booking, double-book, false "booked" or invented price at a client, and what happened (refund, apology, churn)?
  (2) How do you prove to clients that the AI works today?
  (3) What do you pay Cekura, Hamming or anyone for QA?
  (4) Would you pay $49 per client per month for a gate plus a proof report, and who signs?
  Log every answer verbatim.
- Gate A target: 25 calls and at least 8 stress tests run on live agents.

Weeks 5-8 (9 Dec to ~8 Jan, Gate B):
- Send each stress-tested agency its scored report, framed as "X% of hostile calls produced a wrong commitment; here is the fix live on your agent in one afternoon".
- Offer the €750, 60-day, 5-agent pilot with a one-page order form and card collected via a Stripe payment link. Use test-to-live keys only for this invoice.
- Ask the 3 warmest agencies for a pilot. Offer founder-installed setup over Christmas, a quiet period for agencies, so setup costs them nothing.
- Gate B pass: at least 1 signed and paid pilot (target 2-3), plus at least 1 end client who agreed to receive the proof report.
- Build v1 in the 4 weeks after the first signature, on the pilot's actual platform first.
designs.kill_criteria:
Kill or re-pivot if any of these hold by 8 Jan 2027:
- Fewer than 8 of 25 agency calls report a concrete wrong-commitment incident at a client in the last 90 days, or most say "we already fixed it with a token gate or GHL native".
- Stress tests on at least 8 live agents find wrong commitments in under 5% of adversarial calls on average. That would mean the pain is mostly solved by platforms and prompts.
- Zero agencies pay the €750 pilot after at least 10 stress-test reports are delivered, or the stated willingness to pay clusters below $20 per client per month (the RingLogix MSP anchor).
- Agencies want only the proof report and not the gate (and vice versa). In that case narrow to that half rather than kill, but only if someone pays for it.
- Within the pilot: fewer than 2 caught mismatches per client per month, or the pilot agency does not convert at the 60-day mark.
designs.path_to_scale:
Path in four stages:
1. Agency wedge, 2027. Target 100 agencies with an average of 8 client agents at about $40, roughly $400k ARR. That is a solid seed story, not venture scale by itself.
2. Embed in white-label voice platforms and MSP telecom resellers: Trillet-type platforms, RingLogix-type MSPs, and UCaaS add-ons. Price per agent at volume. This reaches tens of thousands of SMB agents with snuepi as the "verified commitments" layer.
3. Widen the surfaces and the commitments. Cover chat, SMS and email agents, and the vertical receptionist vendors who lack it. Expand from bookings and prices to deposits and no-show fees (the parked Stripe Connect code), cancellations, refunds and policy promises. Snuepi becomes the system of record for "what any AI may promise on behalf of this business". The terms layer and connectors are the asset.
4. Monetize the evidence. The signed commitment history plus measured error rates become the data feed that AI-liability insurers and MGAs need for underwriting and parametric triggers (Armilla, Testudo, HSB via carriers, AIUC-1 audits), alongside an EU compliance angle: OLG Hamm attributes chatbot statements to the operator, and the Digital Fairness Act is coming. Insurers or agencies could subsidise or require the layer, a premium-credit distribution loop.

Venture outcome: the trust and commitment layer between every SMB and the AI agents speaking for it. The open question is whether stages 2-4 materialise. Stage 1 alone is a good small business.
designs.biggest_risk:
Willingness to pay for a separate reliability layer is unproven. Builders treat these failures as debugging problems they can fix with a token gate and prompt tricks. Platforms (Retell, Vapi, GHL native) keep chipping away at the date and double-booking cases. Agencies attribute churn to "perception" rather than wrong bookings. So the gate alone may be a feature agencies won't pay for.

Mitigations:
- Lead with the client-facing proof report, which targets the stated cause of churn, while the gate keeps the report credible.
- Price low enough to resell.
- The free stress test turns abstract risk into a number for the agency's own agent.
- Hold the kill criteria strictly.

Secondary risks:
- Snuepi's connectors have never touched a real calendar or booking system. Validate live early.
- Agency segments are crowded with low-margin MSP pricing ($75-150 per agent) that compresses the price.

designs.user: The agency's builder or engineer, who swaps the agent's booking and pricing tools for snuepi endpoints and reads mismatch alerts. A secondary user, view-only, is the agency's SMB client (clinic, salon, trades): they get a white-label weekly "what your AI committed to" report.
designs.problem_evidence: Builders report the pain over and over: wrong year or date (vapi.ai/community/m/1379750706482909185), relative dates 1-2 days off (m/1375475162551554108), UTC/Eastern mismatch reporting booked slots as free (support.vapi.ai/t/33208523), double-booking (m/1376589305715359877; support.vapi.ai/t/29168749), and "you're booked" after the webhook failed (support.vapi.ai/t/27162858). Retell agents invent prices (community.retellai.com/t/3393), hit "Time range is in the past", and loop on check_availability (t/3496, Aug 2026). The same failures show up on n8n and Skool (27-comment reschedule/cancel thread). Vapi's own docs say "Prompts guide the model, but they don't enforce approval... enforce it in your service" (docs.vapi.ai/gpt-live/tools). Builders hand-roll a booking_token gate (support.vapi.ai/t/22800021; Reddit 2026-05-22). Radar TRUE GAP 26.8 scores pain 4, frequency 4, WTP 3. Its counter-check found that even ElevenLabs Guardrails 2.0 is not grounded in live calendar or price data, runs only inside ElevenLabs, and keeps no record reconciling what was said with what was booked. Liability is moving toward the operator: OLG Hamm, 12 May 2026, attributes chatbot statements to the business regardless of disclaimers, and IHKs warn about Abmahnungen. There are invented-price cases at SMB level (£89 boiler quote; UK 80% discount on £8k). Price anchors: Cekura $500/mo Startup or $0.05 per monitored call; agency retainers $497-$997/mo; agency pricing guides show $300-500/mo add-ons. Honest caveats: (1) I found no first-person post from an agency that lost a client over a wrong booking. Vendors put 70-80% of churn down to "perception", though they also say clients who can see a booking dashboard cancel less, which supports the client-report piece. (2) WTP for a runtime gate is inferred, not observed. (3) Almost all of this is search snippets.
designs.product:
v1 has three parts and nothing else.
(1) GATED TOOLS. These are hosted tool endpoints the agent calls instead of raw calendar tools: resolve_date, check_availability, book, reschedule, cancel and quote. They ship as importable tool JSON for Vapi custom tools and Retell custom functions, a GHL workflow webhook, and an n8n node/HTTP template. resolve_date turns "next Monday at 3" into an ISO time with an offset in the business's time zone, server-side and DST-safe, and returns a read-back sentence. book does a fresh free/busy check at write time, not the hourly poll, then enforces opening hours, holidays, buffers and services from the business's terms. It returns a confirmation_token only after the calendar write succeeds. If the write fails it returns a scripted "I couldn't confirm that, let me take your details" line. quote returns only prices and discounts from the signed per-client price list. Anything outside it returns "a team member will confirm the price", and the model never computes a price.
(2) END-OF-CALL RECONCILIATION. The Vapi/Retell end-of-call webhook (or an hourly log pull) runs the reply guard over the transcript. It flags any "you're booked / confirmed" with no matching token, any spoken date or time that differs from the booked one, any price or discount not on the list, and any promise outside terms. Alerts go to the agency by email or Slack within minutes. A 30-day backfill of this same pass is the free "Commitment Audit" used for selling.
(3) RECEIPTS. Each gated commitment is written to the signed hash-chained record (what was offered, under which terms version, what was booked). A white-label weekly client report shows bookings made, commitments blocked or corrected, and zero unverified promises. An evidence export is available per booking.
v1 calendars: Google, Microsoft, Cal.com, plus the GHL calendar API (new). EU hosting. Multi-client agency dashboard with simple roles and 2FA.
designs.distribution: 1) Go direct to the exact people who posted the pain. Repurpose the snuepi-signals collector to Vapi/Retell/n8n community, Skool AI Automation Society and GHL Ideas threads about wrong dates, double-booking or invented prices, and offer each poster a free 30-day Commitment Audit of their real call logs (read-only API key). 2) Skool agency communities: a free "booking-safe receptionist" tool template and teardown posts with real audit stats. 3) Integration listings: the GHL Marketplace app, an n8n community node, and a listing in the Vapi/Retell partner directories and template galleries. 4) Later, partnerships with white-label platforms (Trillet-style, MSP resellers such as RingLogix) who resell to hundreds of agencies, and with QA vendors (Cekura/Hamming find failures offline, snuepi blocks them live).
designs.pricing: Per gated client agent: EUR 39/mo (up to 500 gated calls) or EUR 79/mo (unlimited calls, white-label client report, evidence export). Agency minimum EUR 149/mo. Overage EUR 0.04 per gated call, which is under Cekura's $0.05 per monitored call. Commitment Audit: free once, then EUR 290 per audit for agencies onboarding new clients. Pilot offer for Gate B: EUR 490 for 60 days covering up to 5 client agents, credited against the first year. The logic: it is 4-15% of a $497-$997 retainer, so the agency marks it up or bundles it as "booking guarantee". It stays below Cekura's $500 Startup plan for small agencies. The low end (MSP $75-150/agent) is served later through OEM per-call pricing, not this list price.
designs.moat: Honest view: the moat is moderate, and the absorption risk is about 3/5. Retell has shipped current-time variables and a duplicate-call fix, GHL claims native double-booking prevention, and ElevenLabs has runtime guardrails. Why platforms do not fully absorb it: (a) Vapi deliberately pushes enforcement to "your service". Platforms sell minutes and model flexibility, not business-rule correctness, and they will not maintain each SMB's price list, deposit rules and terms. (b) Agencies run several platforms, and snuepi is one gate and one terms file across Vapi, Retell, GHL and n8n, which no single platform will build. (c) Grounding is the hard part, and snuepi already has it tested: live free/busy, DST-safe relative dates, opening hours and holidays, and deterministic price and discount rules. Content guardrails like ElevenLabs and Retell's Feb 2026 release do not check live data. (d) Reconciliation needs both the transcript and the system of record, and only a layer that sits on the tool path sees both. What compounds: a per-client structured terms and price file that agencies do not want to re-enter elsewhere (switching cost); a cross-platform library of failure patterns from every audited and reconciled call, which improves the guard and becomes sellable test suites; and a signed commitment record. As OLG Hamm-style liability and performance-triggered insurance (Armilla, Testudo, AIUC-1, Munich Re aiSure) need measured, verifiable records, that history becomes underwriting data platforms do not hold neutrally. Signed receipts alone are commoditizing (IETF draft, Signet), so the record is a supporting asset, not the moat.
designs.snuepi_reuse: Roughly 60-70% of v1 code already exists and is tested. Booking engine: free-time lookup, book, cancel, move, opening hours, holidays and DST-safe zones are the core of the gated tools, about 30% of v1. Terms layer: price floors, discount/negotiation rules computed deterministically, deposits and request types, plus the 9 sector defaults to seed client setup, about 10%. Reply guard post-filter: false "you're booked", promised discounts and outside links, in 12 languages, retargeted to transcript reconciliation, about 10%. Connectors: Google, Microsoft and Cal.com calendar plus write-back queue, about 8% (add GHL calendar and a fresh free/busy check at write time instead of the hourly poll). Signed hash-chained record, Merkle root, verifier and per-booking evidence bundle, about 7%. One-approval activation: website reading for services, prices and hours to draft each client's price list, about 5%. Hostile-agent and booking simulators repurposed as pre-launch scenario tests, about 3%. snuepi-signals as the lead engine for validation. New work: Vapi/Retell/GHL/n8n tool adapters and webhooks, transcript ingestion, agency multi-tenant dashboard with roles and 2FA, white-label report.
designs.retire: Freeze, don't delete: tag the repo so the inbound-agent vision can be revived when that traffic exists. Retire: the planned chargeback dispute-pack pivot (no observed losses, incumbents such as Chargebacks911 are already selling indemnity and permission trails, and spend is a % of recovered disputes); all public "doors" (phone via Twilio/Telnyx/SignalWire, email door, booking page, website widget, agent card); MCP 31-tool marketplace surface, A2A, ACP, UCP, OAuth customer mandates; money layer (Stripe Connect deposits, SPT, AP2) except for keeping deposit rules as data in terms; identity stack (Web Bot Auth, fake-brand detection, KYA/KYB, Visa/Skyfire tokens, fraud score); goods/products/B2B quotes/cases/consultations flows; phrase-matching regulated guardrails, which over-refuse; restaurant and appointment-system connectors that need partner approval or polling (Phorest, Mindbody, Vagaro, TheFork, OpenTable, resOS, Formitable, Square, Acuity, SimplyBook, Calendly, Setmore, ERP) until a paying agency asks; the 48-business world simulator; public terms registry and "Agent Terms v1" standard work; Norway leftovers. Target: cut from 444 routes to about 40.
designs.validation_plan:
Rule: sell before building. The only pre-sale build is the Commitment Audit, which is the existing reply guard plus Vapi/Retell call-log pull plus calendar compare, about 5 working days, run by hand.
Weeks of 9-16 Nov: retarget snuepi-signals to the pain threads above. Build a list of 120 agencies (posters in Vapi/Retell/n8n forums, Skool AI Automation Society members selling receptionists, UK/DACH/Nordic agencies on GHL). Send 60 personal messages offering a free 30-day audit of real call logs. Write a one-page "booking-safe" teardown with the Vapi docs quote.
By 8 Dec (Gate A, 25 calls): 25 discovery calls with agency owners. Ask Mom-Test questions about the last wrong booking or price, what it cost (refund, client complaint, lost retainer), the current DIY fix (token gate?), and which platforms they use. Ask for log access on the call. Target: 10 audits run on real logs by 12 Dec.
By 19 Dec: deliver each audit as a 1-page report: X false confirmations, Y date/time mismatches, Z off-list prices per 100 booking calls, with call links. Present it live and pitch the EUR 490 / 60-day / 5-client pilot.
By 8 Jan (Gate B): at least 1 signed and paid pilot (target 3), with an invoice issued. Run the pilot first as a concierge: gate one client agent per agency using the existing engine wired by hand to their tool calls, so no new build until payment.
Leading metrics to log: share of agencies whose logs show at least 1 material wrong commitment per 200 booking calls; how many already have a DIY gate; stated price ceiling per client.
designs.kill_criteria: Kill or re-pivot at Gate B if any of these holds. (1) Fewer than 3 of the first 8 real-log audits find at least 1 material wrong commitment (false confirmation, wrong date/time or off-list price) per 200 booking calls, meaning the pain is rare in production. (2) More than half of interviewed agencies already run a working DIY token or conflict gate and say they would not pay to replace it. (3) Fewer than 5 of 25 calls name a price of EUR 39 or more per client per month, or no signed paid pilot exists by 8 Jan 2027. (4) Before Gate B, Vapi or Retell ships a native server-side confirm/conflict/price gate grounded in live calendar and price-list data that covers more than 70% of the audit findings. Partial signal: if agencies want only the audit or monitoring and not the runtime gate, narrow to a reconciliation monitor priced against Cekura, and decide by mid-January.
designs.path_to_scale: Stage 1 (2027): an agency gate on Vapi/Retell/GHL/n8n, aiming for 100 agencies x 10 client agents x about EUR 60 = about EUR 0.7M ARR. Stage 2: OEM per-call pricing to white-label receptionist platforms and MSP voice resellers, plus the GHL Marketplace. One integration reaches thousands of agents. Expand the commitments covered beyond bookings to deposits, refunds, discounts, quotes and order changes for chat and email agents (the same terms engine). Stage 3: become the system of record for what an SMB's AI is allowed to commit to and what it actually committed to, across every agent vendor. Sell that history as audit and underwriting data to AI-liability insurers and MGAs (Armilla, Testudo, HSB-via-carriers, AIUC-1 certification), possibly with lower premiums for gated agents and a compliance pack for EU operators under OLG Hamm-style liability and the Digital Fairness Act. Stage 4: when third-party consumer agents start calling and booking SMBs in volume, the same per-business terms, gated tools and record serve them too, which is the original snuepi vision now arriving with an installed base instead of zero traffic.
designs.biggest_risk: The pain is real for builders but may not translate into a separate budget. Competent agencies fix it with a cheap DIY token/conflict gate or a prompt fix. Platforms (Retell changelog, GHL native double-booking prevention, ElevenLabs Guardrails) keep absorbing the obvious pieces. Agency churn is driven mostly by perceived ROI, not wrong commitments. That could leave snuepi as a nice-to-have at the point where agencies sell at the $75-150/agent low end. The audit-first validation exists to test exactly this on real logs before any build. A secondary risk is market fit for a Europe-first solo founder, because most of these agencies are US-based and EU data residency is not their buying criterion.

designs.name: snuepi Commit: an independent commitment gate and ledger for customer-facing AI agents
designs.one_liner: One drop-in tool URL for Vapi, Retell, GHL and n8n agents. It checks every date, slot, price, discount and policy promise against the business's live calendar and signed terms before the agent says it. It then reconciles what the agent said against what was actually written, and gives the agency a monthly Commitment Accuracy Report to hand to each client.
designs.buyer: The founder or owner of a voice/chat AI agency (2-20 staff) that resells AI receptionists to SMBs at $297-$997+/mo per client (UK/US Skool agencies charge GBP 750-3,000/mo). Start with EU and UK agencies (Germany, Netherlands, Nordics, UK), where OLG Hamm (May 2026) and the IHK warnings create an operator-liability story, then move to US agencies. A secondary buyer for data partnerships, not v1 revenue, is the underwriting lead at an AI-liability MGA or insurer (Armilla, Testudo, AIUC, Mosaic/aiSure).
designs.user: Two users. The agency builder who wires the tool into each client's agent and watches the mismatch feed. The SMB owner (dental clinic, salon, trades, clinic, restaurant) who gets the monthly report and the owner alerts ('your agent quoted EUR 89, your list says EUR 120: corrected/escalated').
designs.problem_evidence: Pain is strong and repeated, but at the builder level. (1) False confirmation. Vapi support 'agent says appointment booked when it was not' (support.vapi.ai/t/27162858). The webhook failed but the agent 'thinks it has successfully booked'. (2) Wrong or past dates and time zones. 'assistant had the correct current time, but the booking request still used a 2024 timestamp' (vapi.ai/community/m/1379750706482909185). The calendar tool returned UTC while the agent reasoned in Eastern and 'reported booked slots as free' (support.vapi.ai/t/33208523). 'Monday' was resolved 1-2 days off (vapi.ai/community/m/1375475162551554108). Retell's own guide calls 'Time range is in the past' a common error. n8n dental workflows book wrong days (community.n8n.io/t/259554). (3) Double booking. Vapi's create-event tool has no conflict detection (support.vapi.ai/t/29168749). Skool and GHL Ideas requests ask to 'recognize existing appointments' (highlevel.canny.io). (4) Invented prices. Retell: 'Agent does not check KB for prices... hallucination close to real thing' (community.retellai.com/t/3393). An SMB AI receptionist quoted GBP 89 when that was not the owner's price (lilachbullock.com). (5) Platforms concede the architecture. Vapi docs say 'Prompts guide the model, but they don't enforce approval... enforce it in your service' (docs.vapi.ai/gpt-live/tools). Builders hand-roll 'confirm only when booking_token exists' gates (reddit snapshot 1tfc3ps; support.vapi.ai/t/22800021). (6) Liability is moving to the operator: Moffatt v Air Canada, BMW Toronto (about C$5-7k honoured, 2026-06), Priceline Penny, OLG Hamm 4 UKl 3/25 (disclaimers did not protect the operator), and German IHK Abmahnung warnings. Honoured promises are generally uninsurable (ISO GenAI exclusions, Jan 2026). (7) Willingness to pay is indirect. Agencies already pay for QA: Cekura charges $0.05/monitored call or $500/mo, and Hamming has an agency tier. Agency guides leave $300-500/mo add-on headroom per client. Counter-evidence I take seriously: (a) I found no first-person case of an agency losing a client over a wrong commitment, and vendors attribute 70-80% of churn to 'perception' and unclear ROI (Trillet). (b) Competent builders fix double-booking in-house. (c) GHL claims native double-booking prevention, and Retell shipped time variables (Mar 2026) and a duplicate-booking fix (Aug 2026). The design answers (a) by selling visibility. The Accuracy Report is the anti-perception-churn artefact: MyVoiceAIConnect says 'clients who can see their booking dashboard are much less likely to cancel'. It answers (b) and (c) by putting most of the value in prices, discounts, policy and reconciliation, which no platform does, not in the date-bug slice.
designs.product: Three parts, nothing else. (A) Commitment tools. One hosted endpoint per client, exposed as Vapi/Retell custom tools, an MCP server, an n8n/Make HTTP node and a GHL custom webhook action. resolve_time(phrase, caller_tz) returns a validated ISO slot plus a read-back sentence. It uses the business time zone, today's date, opening hours, holidays and DST, and rejects past dates and weekday/date mismatches. check_and_hold(slot) runs live free/busy against Google, Microsoft, Cal.com or the GHL calendar and returns a short-lived hold token. book(hold_token) returns a booking_token and the exact 'say this' confirmation only after the calendar write is verified. quote(service) and offer(discount) return the price from the business's signed price list and a discount only within its configured authority; anything else returns 'escalate to human'. reschedule/cancel cover the Skool-reported gap. (B) Reconciliation. After each call, an end-of-call-report webhook (Vapi/Retell transcript plus tool log) runs the existing post-guard over the transcript. It flags 'said booked without a booking_token', 'stated a price or discount not issued by quote/offer', 'stated a date or time different from the ledger' and 'unhandled reschedule'. It alerts the agency in Slack or email within a minute and, if configured, the owner. Real-time voice blocking is explicitly out of scope for v1. (C) Ledger and report. Every issued commitment and every mismatch is a signed, hash-chained entry with the price-list and terms version hash. The per-client dashboard shows commitments made, verified, flagged and corrected, and a monthly white-label PDF Commitment Accuracy Report goes to the SMB. Setup reuses the website reader to propose the price list, hours and discount rules for one-click approval. A 'commitment audit' mode runs (B) offline over 50-200 historical transcripts plus a calendar export. This is the sales hook and works before anything is installed.
designs.distribution: 1) Concierge 'free commitment audit' offered in Skool communities (AI Automation Society, voice-agency groups), Vapi and Retell Discord/forums, and the n8n community. Reply directly to the threads cited above with a working resolver plus the audit offer. The existing snuepi-signals collector finds these threads daily. 2) Listings: a Vapi tool template or snippet, a Retell custom-function template, an n8n community node, then a GHL Marketplace app (white-label friendly, so agencies can rebrand the report). 3) Agency-to-SMB is the channel: each agency carries 5-50 clients, so one sale lands many seats. 4) Later: Retell/Vapi partner or expert directories, and a co-marketing route with an AI-liability MGA ('agents running the gate get evidence your underwriter can read').
designs.pricing: Per client agent per month, billed to the agency, which resells it. Starter EUR 29 (tools plus reconciliation on up to 300 calls). Pro EUR 79 (up to 1,500 calls, owner alerts, white-label monthly report, signed ledger export). Overage EUR 0.03/call, below Cekura's $0.05/monitored call. Agency bundle EUR 290/mo for 10 client agents. The commitment audit is free for the first 50 transcripts, or EUR 300 for a full 200-call audit credited against a pilot. Pilot offer for Gate B: EUR 1,500 for 90 days, covering up to 5 client agents of one agency, with a written conversion price. This sits inside the $30-500/mo reliability-spend range implied by Cekura and the agency-margin data, and below 10% of a typical $497-997 retainer.
designs.moat: Honest view first: the date and time-zone slice will be absorbed within 12 months. Retell already ships time variables and duplicate-call fixes, GHL claims native double-booking prevention, and ElevenLabs Guardrails 2.0 blocks text-rule discounts inside ElevenLabs. Those are features, not the business. What platforms do not absorb within 2 years, and why: (1) Neutrality. A record of what the agent promised, kept by the vendor whose agent promised it, is self-graded evidence. An SMB facing an Abmahnung or a disputed discount, and an insurer running performance-triggered cover (Armilla) or parametric cover (aiSure) where the threshold is 'checked against real-world outcomes', need an independent third-party record. Vapi, OpenAI and GHL are structurally conflicted here. (2) Cross-platform. Agencies run Vapi plus Retell plus GHL plus n8n and switch platforms often. Each platform polices only its own channel and has 'little incentive to police the promises its agents make' (market-gaps absorption note). The gate and ledger move with the agency across platforms, which builds switching cost on our side. (3) Grounding in the business's own systems of record: per-business signed terms, price lists, discount authority, and connectors to calendars and booking systems. Platforms leave this to prompts by design ('enforce it in your service'). Stripe, Cloudflare and Shopify are not in this lane. (4) The compounding asset. Every call adds a labelled pair (what was said, what was true) across platforms, models and verticals. That produces better resolvers and, more importantly, the only cross-platform actuarial dataset of SMB agent commitment-error rates. This is what insurers and certifiers (AIUC-1-style audits) lack. Over time, per-agency and per-agent accuracy history becomes a portable credential that is costly to leave behind. Commoditised parts (hash chains, receipts: Signet, ActionProof, the IETF draft) are inputs, not the moat. The receipt proves integrity. The value is the correctness check against business truth.
designs.snuepi_reuse: I estimate existing snuepi code covers about 60-65% of v1. Carried over: the booking engine core (free-time lookup, hold/confirm, opening hours, holidays, DST-safe time zones, cancel/move), which becomes resolve_time, check_and_hold, book and reschedule. The reply guard post-guard ('false you're booked', promised discounts), which becomes the transcript reconciler, minus the 12-language and cost-cap extras unless needed. The terms layer (price lists, price floors, deterministic negotiation and discount rules, signing, sector defaults), which becomes the quote/offer authority. The Google, Microsoft and iCal calendar connectors plus Cal.com (others later). The signed hash-chained record and Merkle root plus public verification, which becomes the ledger. The MCP server, cut down from 31 tools to about 7, plus REST/OpenAPI. One-approval activation (website reader). The booking simulator and hostile-agent test run, repurposed as a pre-install self-test that fires 30 adversarial date and discount prompts at the agency's agent. New build: Vapi and Retell end-of-call webhook adapters and tool templates, a GHL calendar connector and webhook action, a transcript-to-ledger claim extractor (an LLM extracts claims, the deterministic engine judges them), an agency multi-tenant dashboard with 2FA and roles, the PDF report, and Stripe billing.

The evidence shows no observed agent-dispute losses, Instant Checkout scaled back, budget paid per recovered dispute, and Chargebacks911, Visa and Chargeflow already in that lane. Freeze and archive: phone/email doors and the Twilio/Telnyx/SignalWire/Azure speech stack (agencies already own the voice layer, and it would be a latency rabbit hole); the booking page and widget; ACP, UCP, A2A, AP2 and Stripe SPT agent payments; Stripe Connect deposits and no-show money flows (re-add later as 'deposit-gated booking' only if pilots ask); Web Bot Auth, fake-brand detection, KYA/KYB and outside identity tokens (keep the code for a phase-3 inbound-agent door, not v1); consultations, multi-day cases, request_quotes and B2B catalogue/ERP; the regulated-work phrase guardrails that over-refuse; Phorest, Mindbody, Vagaro, resOS, Formitable, TheFork and OpenTable connectors; the 48-business world simulator; the public Agent Terms registry as a marketing surface; Norway leftovers; and most of the 444 routes and 40+ rule options. (4) No signed, priced pilot of at least EUR 1,500 by 8 Jan 2027 (Gate B).
