designs.path_to_scale: Phase 1 (2027 H1): agencies on Vapi, Retell, GHL and n8n. 20 agencies x 15 client agents x EUR 60 is about EUR 216k ARR. Prove that the Accuracy Report reduces client churn. Phase 2: widen the channels and commitment types to chat, WhatsApp and email agents and to Intercom/Zendesk-style bots, and add refund and policy claims grounded in the business's own policy text. Sell direct to multi-location SMB groups (dental and clinic chains) and to vertical receptionist vendors as an embedded 'verified commitments' API. Phase 3, the venture-scale part: the ledger becomes the neutral system of record for what AI agents promised on behalf of businesses. Two moves follow. (a) An insurer and certifier channel: carriers and MGAs use per-agent commitment-accuracy history for eligibility, pricing and parametric triggers, which unlocks cover for agent-made commitments that is currently uninsurable (ISO exclusions, honour-the-promise losses), with revenue share per insured agent. (b) An inbound-agent door: when third-party consumer agents (ChatGPT, Gemini, Alexa) start booking and buying from SMBs at volume, the same terms, gate and ledger serve them. That reuses snuepi's parked identity, mandate and payment code without betting on it now. The compounding cross-platform error dataset supports a standard (an 'AIUC-1 for SMB agent commitments') and a certification badge, which pulls demand from SMBs and insurers back to agencies.
designs.biggest_risk: Willingness to pay is unproven, and the pain may be a 'builder debugging' problem rather than a budget line. I found no first-person evidence of an agency losing a client or money over a wrong commitment. Vendors attribute churn to perception and ROI. Technical agencies fix double-booking with a token gate in their own code. Platforms keep chipping off the date slice (Retell Mar/Aug 2026, GHL native, ElevenLabs Guardrails 2.0). If what remains (price, discount and policy checks plus reconciliation) does not register as urgent, this becomes a EUR 29 nice-to-have with high churn and no route to the insurer data asset. A secondary risk: the core agency market is US-heavy and price-compressed at the low end (white-label agents at $75-150/mo), which conflicts with the EU-first constraint. The plan mitigates both by running free audits that measure real error rates before any build, and by keeping kill criteria tied to those numbers.

designs.name: Kept (a snuepi rework): independent booking-truth verification and client proof reports for voice-AI agencies
designs.one_liner: After every call, Kept checks what a client's Vapi, Retell or GHL agent promised (time, date, time zone, price, discount) against the real calendar and price list. It alerts the agency within minutes when a "you're booked" or a quote is false, and gives the agency a white-label monthly report proving every booking was real. Agencies use that report to keep clients.
designs.buyer: The founder or owner of a small voice/chat-AI agency with 3 to 40 SMB client accounts. These agencies resell receptionists for $297-$997/mo (some UK/US agencies charge £750-£3,000/mo), mostly in the UK, US and EU. The buyer pays from the gross margin on the retainer, since platform cost is about $0.105-$0.11/min. Second buyer type: white-label agency-platform vendors (Trillet, MyVoiceAIConnect type), which could resell Kept to their agencies.
designs.user: Day to day: the agency's builder/ops person, who gets the alerts, fixes the flow and looks at the error list. The agency's SMB client (clinic, salon, trades, dental, auto) also uses it passively: they read the white-label monthly "verified bookings and value" report, and that is where retention is won or lost.
designs.problem_evidence: Why not the obvious "commitment firewall" (inline gate): the evidence supports the pain at builder level, but not an agency paying for an inline gate. (a) Builders hand-roll the token gate themselves: "agent may confirm only when a booking token is present" (support.vapi.ai/t/22800021; Reddit snapshot 1tfc3ps, 2026-05). (b) Platforms are absorbing it piece by piece: Vapi tool rejection plans (Aug 2025), Retell timezone variables (Mar 2026) and duplicate-booking fix (Aug 2026), GHL's claimed native double-booking prevention, ElevenLabs Guardrails 2.0. (c) No first-person post shows an agency losing a client over a wrong booking. Two pieces of evidence point at an observer that proves outcomes. First, Trillet: 70-80% of agency client cancellations are "perception churn". Second, MyVoiceAIConnect (~2026-11-08): "clients who can see their booking dashboard are much less likely to cancel because the AI doesn't feel like a black box". Third, Roark (~2026-09): "a wrong-timezone booking can pass as a 'success' in a 95% booking rate until the patient complains weeks later". That failure is silent, and only a ground-truth comparison catches it. The failure classes are documented repeatedly: false "you're booked" when the webhook failed (support.vapi.ai/t/27162858), UTC vs local tz reporting busy slots as free (support.vapi.ai/t/33208523), relative dates 1-2 days off (vapi.ai/community/m/1375475162551554108), double-booking despite tz plus injected time (vapi.ai/community/m/1376589305715359877), "Time range is in the past" (Retell community), invented prices close to real ones (community.retellai.com/t/.../3393), £89 invented boiler price (Lilach Bullock 2026), and reschedule/cancel failures (Skool AI Automation Society, 27 comments). Vapi's docs, "enforce it in your service", confirm that the platform will not verify outcomes for the agency. Willingness to pay is indirect only. Anchors: Cekura $0.05/monitored call or $500/mo Startup; agency management fees of $1-3k/mo per client leave room for $25-80 per client. No direct WTP evidence exists for this product, and validation has to supply it. The dispute pack is the weakest option: there are no observed agent chargebacks, ChatGPT Instant Checkout was scaled back (~Mar 2026), and Chargebacks911 already sells indemnity plus permission-trail records. Dispute budgets are a share of recovered money (Chargeflow 25%, Disputifier 20%).
designs.product: v1 is observe-first and runs after the call, so it adds no live-call latency or hot-path liability. (1) Connect: the agency pastes a Vapi or Retell API key (or adds an end-of-call webhook) or connects GHL. Per client, it links the calendar or booking system (Google, Microsoft, Cal.com, Acuity, Square, SimplyBook, Calendly via existing connectors; new GHL calendar connector). Activation reads the client's website for services, prices and hours, and the agency sets the maximum allowed discount. (2) Extract commitments from each call's transcript and tool-call log: booking claims (service, date, time, time zone, reschedule, cancel), quoted prices and durations, and offered discounts or refunds. (3) Reconcile against ground truth: does the event exist? Does it match the stated date, time and time zone? Is it in the past, outside opening hours, or double-booked? Did a reschedule actually cancel the old slot? Does the quoted price match the price list? Is the discount within the allowed limit? (4) Alert within 5 minutes by email, Slack or SMS for high-severity mismatches ("told caller Thu 15:00 booked, nothing in calendar"), with a one-click fix link or a call-back task. (5) Agency console: error rate per client and per failure class, with a trend after each prompt or flow change, so they can see whether a fix worked. (6) White-label monthly client report (PDF and link): calls handled, bookings verified as real, estimated booked revenue, errors caught and fixed. This targets the stated churn driver (perception and unclear ROI). Each call's verdict is written to the existing signed hash-chained log, kept internally and not marketed in v1. Not in v1: the inline "verify_and_book" custom tool, which reuses the booking engine and returns a booking token. It comes in v1.5, and only if pilots ask for it after seeing their own error rates.
designs.distribution: Founder-led selling into where agencies already ask for help: Skool AI Automation Society and other agency Skools (Pickup and similar), the Vapi Discord/community, Retell community and n8n forum booking threads. Answer these with real fixes plus the offer of a free "Booking Truth Audit" (we reconcile your last 30 days of calls against the calendar). Use the snuepi-signals lead engine to find fresh threads about wrong bookings or false confirmations. Then: a GHL Marketplace app, Vapi/Retell integration listings, and a reseller deal with one white-label agency platform (Trillet or MyVoiceAIConnect type, since they already publish that dashboards reduce churn). The client-facing report spreads Kept on its own: each report goes to an SMB owner with "verified by Kept" on it.
designs.pricing: Free audit (concierge) as the lead magnet. Agency plan at €199/mo including 5 client accounts, then €29 per client account per month. Above 2,000 calls per client per month, €0.02 per verified call. The design-partner pilot is €249/mo flat for up to 10 client accounts, on a 90-day term, signed. Anchors: Cekura $0.05/call or $500/mo; per-client cost of about €29 is 3-6% of a $497-$997 retainer. The agency marks it up and resells it as a "verified bookings guarantee". The v1.5 inline booking tool would be a +€15 per client add-on.
designs.moat: Why the platforms do not absorb it: (1) Vapi, Retell, GHL and ElevenLabs each grade only their own channel and have little incentive to tell an agency's client that their agent made errors. An independent outside verifier is the point, and an agency running a mix of platforms needs one view across all of them. Vapi's own docs push verification onto the builder. (2) It checks against the client's systems of record (20 calendar and booking connectors, price list, hours, DST-safe time logic), which voice platforms do not own. (3) Cekura, Hamming and Coval test builds before and around launch, for builders. Kept verifies real outcomes after the fact and reports them to the end client, so its job is retention, not QA. It could still be copied, so speed into the agency channel matters. What compounds over time: a labelled corpus of real commitment failures across platforms, sectors and calendars, which sharpens extraction and becomes per-sector rule packs and benchmarks ("your agent's verified-booking rate vs. dental average"). Switching costs come from white-label reports embedded in the agency-client relationship. A per-agent "Kept score" history becomes the verified performance data that performance-triggered and parametric AI insurers (Armilla, Munich Re aiSure/Mosaic, AIUC-1) need and cannot get from SMBs today. Honest caveat: in year one the moat is mostly speed and channel, not technology.
designs.snuepi_reuse: Kept reuses roughly 50-60% of v1 from snuepi. Booking engine time logic: opening hours, holidays, DST-safe time zones and slot validation, which becomes the ground-truth checker. Connectors: Google, Microsoft and iCal calendars, Cal.com, Acuity, Square, SimplyBook, Calendly and Setmore, plus the sync and polling code. Reply-guard post-guard patterns that detect false "you're booked", promised discounts and prices, in 12 languages, repurposed from blocking to extraction and flagging. Terms layer: price floors, discount rules and sector defaults (9), used as the client's price-list and discount policy. One-approval activation (website scrape of services, prices and hours). Signed hash-chained record plus Merkle root, used as an internal per-call verdict log. Booking simulation and hostile-agent simulators, used to make synthetic test calls for regression. Daily cost caps for the LLM extraction. Fly.io, SQLite and Litestream infra plus the Scaleway EU LLM. New work: Vapi, Retell and GHL call-log ingestors, a GHL calendar connector, the commitment-extraction pipeline, the alerting layer, the agency console and the white-label report.
designs.retire: Drop the planned agent-purchase dispute pack and everything aimed at outside buyer agents: ACP, UCP, AP2 mandates, Stripe shared payment tokens, OAuth customer mandates, A2A, the 31-tool MCP buyer-agent server and per-business agent cards. Drop the money stack (deposits, no-show fees, Stripe Connect, chargeback alerts), the Web Bot Auth, KYA/KYB, fake-brand detection and trust-level identity stack, and the phone, email, booking-page and widget doors. Also drop the regulated-work phrase guardrails, the 48-business world simulator, the free terms registry and the "Agent Terms v1" standard work (park in a public repo), the Phorest, Mindbody and Vagaro partner-gated connectors, the restaurant connectors (resOS, Formitable, TheFork, OpenTable) unless a pilot needs one, and the Norway leftovers. Cut from 444 routes and 40+ rule options to about 25 routes. Keep code in git, and remove it from the deployed product.
designs.validation_plan: The concierge audit is both the sales motion and the evidence test. Week of 9 Nov: freeze the live product. Build a CLI audit script in 4-5 days that imports Vapi/Retell call exports and the tool-call log, reads the client calendar through existing connectors, extracts commitments (reply-guard patterns plus LLM) and outputs a mismatch report. Run it on your own snuepi simulations, and label the results as simulated. 9 Nov-8 Dec (Gate A, 25 calls): post useful fixes in 2-3 booking threads a day across the Vapi community, Retell community, n8n forum and Skool AI Automation Society, and DM UK/US/EU agency owners found by snuepi-signals and Skool member lists. On each call ask: how many client accounts and which platforms, the last time a wrong or false booking reached a client and how they found out, what it cost them, what they send clients each month as proof, whether they have lost a client and why, and what they pay Cekura or Hamming or anyone else for reliability. Close each call by asking for a free 30-day Booking Truth Audit on one client account (read-only API key plus calendar read). Targets by 8 Dec: 25 calls, at least 10 audit agreements, at least 5 audits delivered. Each audit goes back as a white-label sample report, and the founder records the real mismatch rate per failure class. 9 Dec-8 Jan (Gate B): for each audit that found a mismatch rate of at least 1% of booking calls, or at least one false "you're booked", present findings live and ask for the €249/mo, 90-day pilot covering up to 10 clients, starting mid-January and billed by Stripe invoice. Run the 6-week v1 build only after the first signature. Gate B passes with at least 1 signed, priced pilot (target 3). In parallel, open one conversation with a white-label agency-platform vendor about reselling, as a second signal, not a substitute. Report simulated and real numbers separately in every update.
designs.kill_criteria: Kill or pivot if any of these happens. (1) Across at least 5 real audits, wrong or false commitments are under 0.5% of booking calls and no audit finds a false "you're booked". That means prompt tricks and native fixes already work and there is nothing to sell. (2) Fewer than 6 of 25 agencies will grant read-only log and calendar access for a free audit. That means the trust or friction barrier is too high for an observer. (3) Zero signed, priced pilots by 8 Jan 2027, or every agency caps willingness to pay below €10 per client per month. (4) Agencies say the client report adds nothing because their platform's dashboard already convinces clients. (5) Vapi, Retell or GHL ships native post-call booking reconciliation against the calendar before Gate B. In that case, check whether an inline cross-platform tool still has demand before continuing.
designs.path_to_scale: Stage 1 (2027): voice-AI agencies, bookings first, then prices, discounts, reschedules and cancellations. Aim for 100 agencies and 1,500 client accounts at about €30 each, roughly €0.5M ARR. Stage 2: add chat, WhatsApp and email agents and policy or refund claims (the EU angle: OLG Hamm May 2026 holds the business liable for its chatbot's statements, and German IHKs warn about Abmahnungen). Add the inline verify_and_book tool and marketplace listings on GHL, Vapi, Retell and ElevenLabs. Stage 3: sell an OEM or API to vertical receptionist vendors and booking SaaS (Cal.com, SimplyBook, Phorest type), who need independent proof that bookings are real, and to white-label agency platforms. Stage 4: the per-agent verified-outcome history and signed record become the data layer for AI liability insurers and MGAs (Armilla's performance-triggered cover, Munich Re aiSure/Mosaic parametric, AIUC-1 certification, Testudo). That means underwriting scores, claims evidence, and embedded cover for SMB agents ("Kept-verified agents insurable at X"). At that point Kept would be the independent outcome-verification and commitment ledger for the millions of SMB-facing AI agents. The venture-scale case rests on that ledger, not on the agency tool alone.
designs.biggest_risk: The pain may be builder-level debugging rather than an agency budget line. Evidence: no first-person agency churn from wrong commitments, competent builders fix it in their own code, and real error rates after injecting {{now}} and adding a token gate may be too low to justify a monthly fee. A second risk is that Cekura, Roark or the platforms add post-call calendar reconciliation and client reports cheaply. Agency customers are also churny and fad-driven, and the low end of white-label pricing ($75-150 per agent) squeezes the add-on. The concierge audits in Nov-Dec exist to measure this risk directly, on real call logs, before any build.

scores.name: Design 1: BookedRight (fastest-revenue)
scores.fatal_flaw: It tries to do everything in 4 weeks: an inline gate on 4 platforms, post-call reconciliation, a white-label report, a stress tester and 9 booking connectors that have never touched a live system. The core of it is the inline gate, which is the thing builders hand-roll with a booking_token and which Retell, GHL and Vapi are absorbing piece by piece. So the headline product is the most commoditised part, and the plan has the least time to build it properly. The kill bar (8 of 25 calls citing an incident) is soft enough to pass on anecdotes.
scores.best_idea_to_graft: The free Booking Stress Test: about 50 adversarial calls placed against the agency's live phone number or web call. It needs no API key and no log access, so it gets around Kept's biggest friction point (agencies handing over read-only access) and gives the agency a scary number in 48 hours.

scores.name: Design 2: snuepi Commit (max-reuse)
scores.fatal_flaw: The product is a set of gated tools that replace the agent's own booking and pricing tools. That means re-plumbing every client agent, putting snuepi in the live-call hot path with latency and liability, and competing head-on with the DIY token gate and native fixes. The low price (EUR 39 per client, EUR 490 pilot) signals that the team does not believe there is real willingness to pay, and it compresses toward the $75-150 MSP floor.
scores.best_idea_to_graft: A kill criterion that is quantitative and falsifiable: at least 1 material wrong commitment per 200 booking calls on real logs, plus an explicit kill if a native platform gate would cover more than 70% of audit findings. Also the 'concierge gate one client agent by hand' pilot, so the inline gate is only built for agencies that have already paid.

scores.name: Design 3: snuepi Commit, independent ledger (deepest-moat)
scores.fatal_flaw: The moat thesis is that neutral evidence becomes valuable to insurers and to EU liability disputes. No buyer in the evidence has asked for that, and receipts and hash chains are already commoditising (IETF draft, Signet). Spending 10 of the 25 Gate A calls on insurers, SMB end clients and platform partners leaves only 15 agency conversations to prove the one thing that matters, which is agency willingness to pay. A EUR 1,500 pilot for an unproven tool is a high first ask.
scores.best_idea_to_graft: Weight the value toward prices, discounts and policy promises plus reconciliation, the part no platform validates, rather than the date and time-zone slice that will be absorbed within 12 months. Also take the audit metric 'errors per 100 calls the agency had NOT caught', which is the single best number for proving both the pain and the proof-report value, and the willingness to test a higher price point.

scores.name: Design 4: Kept, post-call booking-truth verification (contrarian)
scores.fatal_flaw: An observer only catches errors after the caller has been told something false, and in year one its moat is speed and channel. Cekura ($0.05 per monitored call), Roark and the platforms' own dashboards are one feature away from adding a post-call reconciliation against the calendar plus a client report. It also needs read access to call logs and calendars from agencies that may not trust a solo founder with that, which is the design's own kill criterion 2.
scores.best_idea_to_graft: Sell retention, not QA. The white-label 'verified bookings and value' client report targets the churn driver the evidence actually documents (70-80% of cancellations are perception churn; clients who can see a dashboard cancel less). It runs post-call with no hot-path latency, and the inline gate is held back as a paid v1.5 add-on that only ships when an agency's own error rate justifies it.

judgements.winner: Design 4: Kept, post-call booking-truth verification (contrarian), reworked with grafts from 1, 2 and 3
judgements.rationale: All four designs chase the same wedge: voice-AI agencies, with wrong bookings and invented prices as the pain. All four share the same unproven core: no agency has been observed paying, or churning a client, because of a wrong commitment. So the deciding factor is which design matches the evidence we do have and validates cheapest. That evidence says three things. First, the pain is builder-level and gets fixed in-house with a token gate. Second, platforms keep absorbing the inline-gate slice: Retell's time variables and duplicate-call fix, GHL's claimed native double-booking prevention, Vapi's rejection plans. Third, the churn agencies actually report is 'perception', which visible proof reduces. Designs 1 and 2 lead with the inline gate, which is the most commoditised and most DIY-able part, and it puts a solo founder in the live-call hot path across 4 platforms. Design 3 has the best strategic honesty and the largest scale story, but its moat (insurer-grade neutral ledger data) rests on buyers who have not asked, and it dilutes Gate A away from agencies. Design 4 is the only one built around the documented churn driver. It is the cheapest for a solo founder to ship (post-call, no latency, no re-plumbing of client agents), and its free audit is both the sales motion and the falsification test. Its weaknesses are a thin moat and access friction, both fixable by grafting. The best-fit rework: (1) Run Design 1's no-access Stress Test as the first touch, then Kept's 30-day log audit as the second touch. (2) Report Design 3's 'errors per 100 calls the agency had not caught' as the headline metric, and weight checks toward price, discount and policy promises, not dates. (3) Use Design 2's hard thresholds (1 per 200 calls; a native-gate coverage kill) and its concierge inline gate for pilots only. (4) Raise the pilot from EUR 249 to roughly EUR 500-750 to test real willingness to pay instead of courtesy willingness to pay. (5) Keep the signed ledger internal until an insurer asks. Honest investor verdict: as a business this is a small, fast-to-test bet worth 8 weeks. It becomes fundable only if the audits show error rates that agencies did not know about and at least two agencies pay for the client report specifically.

scores.name: Design 1: BookedRight (fastest-revenue)
scores.fatal_flaw: The sales hook is a synthetic stress test. It shows the agent CAN fail, not that it DOES fail on real client calls, and agencies will wave off 'your agent fails on adversarial DST-week calls' as an edge case. v1 also tries to build the hot-path gate, reconciliation, the white-label report and the stress tester across four platforms and roughly nine untested connectors in 4 weeks. That is overbuilt for one founder and puts snuepi in the live booking path before any trust exists.
scores.best_idea_to_graft: The pilot mechanics: a card on file, a signed one-page order form, and the fee credited against the first months. Also the affiliate cut for Skool course owners as a distribution loop. Keep the synthetic stress test only as a fallback for agencies that refuse read-only log access.

scores.name: Design 2: snuepi Commit (max-reuse)
scores.fatal_flaw: It leads with the runtime gate. That is the exact piece competent builders hand-roll with a booking_token, and the piece Retell, GHL and ElevenLabs keep absorbing. It also asks a churn-averse agency to swap the booking tools on live client agents before snuepi has shown a single error on their own calls. That is a lot of friction on top of the weakest part of the willingness-to-pay story.
scores.best_idea_to_graft: Keep v1 connectors to Google, Microsoft, Cal.com and a new GHL calendar connector, and freeze the rest until a payer asks. Add the paid 'audit per new client onboarding' (EUR 290) as recurring audit revenue. Adopt its kill criterion that triggers if a platform ships a native gate covering more than 70% of findings.

scores.name: Design 3: snuepi Commit ledger (deepest-moat)
scores.fatal_flaw: It optimises for an insurer-data and neutrality moat that has no buyer today. It spends 5 of the 25 Gate A calls on insurers and platforms instead of payers. Its EUR 1,500 pilot is too large an ask for a 1-15 person agency selling $297-997 retainers in a December holiday window. The result is the right long-term story with a short-term sale that is unlikely to close.
scores.best_idea_to_graft: The Gate A metric 'commitment errors per 100 calls that the agency had NOT caught'. This is the number that converts. Also the architecture in which an LLM extracts the claims and the deterministic engine judges them. And the focus on value in prices, discounts and policy promises rather than the date bug, which platforms will absorb.

scores.name: Design 4: Kept (contrarian, observe-first verification + client proof report)
scores.fatal_flaw: Observe-only catches the error after the caller has hung up, so the agency still eats the wrong booking. A post-call monitor plus a dashboard report is also the easiest thing for Cekura, Roark or a platform's own analytics to copy. Without a prevention upsell it risks becoming a EUR 29 nice-to-have with high churn.
scores.best_idea_to_graft: The observe-first motion. Installation is a read-only API key plus calendar read, with no hot-path latency or liability. The free 30-day 'Booking Truth Audit' on real logs doubles as the sales demo and the pain measurement, and the white-label monthly report targets the stated churn driver (perception and unclear ROI).

judgements.winner: Design 4: Kept (contrarian, observe-first verification + client proof report)
judgements.rationale:
I'd choose Design 4 because it fits the evidence best and is the easiest of the four to sell. The evidence says agency churn is about 70-80% 'perception', and that clients who can see a booking dashboard cancel less. Wrong timezone bookings stay invisible until a patient complains, and competent builders already hand-roll the token gate while platforms absorb the date and double-booking pieces. All of that points to a product that checks what the agent said against the real calendar and price list after the call, and gives the agency proof it can show the client. An inline gate points the other way.

Setup is only a read-only API key plus calendar read. For a churny 3-40 client agency in December, that is far easier to say yes to than letting a stranger rewire the booking tools on live agents (D1, D2, D3). The €249/mo flat pilot also fits that buyer better than D3's €1,500 or D1's €750. The concierge audit on real logs tests the core unknown, how often wrong commitments actually happen in production, before any build. Solo feasibility is the highest of the four because there is no booking hot path to own.

Its weakness is that it only detects errors and never prevents them, so the reworked product should graft in the following:
(1) From D2: offer the gated tools (verify_and_book with booking_token, plus quote/offer from the signed price list) as a paid v1.5 upsell, pitched only after an agency has seen its own error rate. That turns the monitor into a prevention purchase. Also limit connectors to Google, Microsoft, Cal.com and GHL, and freeze Acuity, Square and the rest until someone pays.
(2) From D3: lead every audit readout with 'errors per 100 calls that you did not know about'. Weight the product toward prices, discounts and policy promises, because platforms will absorb the date slice within 12 months. Use LLM extraction with a deterministic judge.
(3) From D1: use a card on file and a signed order form for the pilot, with the fee credited on conversion. Keep the synthetic stress test as a fallback for agencies that won't share logs. Use Skool course-owner affiliates for distribution.
(4) From D2: charge a recurring paid audit for each new client an agency onboards.

Keep the signed hash-chained ledger internal as the long-term asset for insurers and MGAs, but don't sell it in year one. Hold D4's kill criteria strictly: fewer than 0.5% wrong commitments across 5 real audits, fewer than 6 of 25 agencies granting log access, or no priced pilot by 8 Jan 2027.

scores.name: BookedRight: a commitment gate and client proof report for voice-agent agencies (snuepi rework)
scores.fatal_flaw: It builds too much on too little proof. In 4 weeks it ships an inline gate on four platforms (Vapi, Retell, GHL, n8n), reconciliation, a white-label report and a stress tester. That 4-week estimate relies on 9 booking connectors that have only ever run against imitations. Its main validation tool, the simulated stress test, measures failures snuepi provokes, not failures real callers hit. So it cannot show whether production error rates justify a fee, which is the question the evidence leaves open. GHL's claimed native double-booking prevention and builders' own token gates already erode the gate.
scores.best_idea_to_graft: A free adversarial stress test as a zero-access opening offer. It needs no logs or API keys, so it can start conversations with agencies that will not yet hand over call data. It is the first step before a real-log audit, not a replacement for one.

scores.name: snuepi Commit: a commitment gate and audit for agency-built voice and chat agents (lens max-reuse)
scores.fatal_flaw: It leads with the hot-path runtime gate, the part the evidence says competent builders already hand-roll (the booking_token gate in Vapi forum thread 22800021 and Reddit 1tfc3ps) and platforms are absorbing piece by piece (Retell time variables in Mar 2026 and its duplicate-call fix in Aug 2026, plus GHL native). It also takes on live-call latency and liability for being wrong. The €490 pilot is too cheap to separate real willingness to pay from politeness.
scores.best_idea_to_graft: Numeric kill criteria tied to real logs: at least 1 material wrong commitment per 200 booking calls in at least 3 of 8 audits, at most half of agencies already running a DIY gate, and an explicit platform-absorption trigger. Also: a fresh free/busy check at write time instead of hourly polling.

scores.name: snuepi Commit: an independent commitment gate and ledger for customer-facing AI agents (lens deepest-moat)
scores.fatal_flaw: Its moat and scale story rest on demand nobody has stated. Insurers need performance data (Armilla, aiSure), but no insurer or managing general agent has asked for SMB commitment ledgers. The SMB cases (UK 80% discount, BMW, Priceline) were settled by refunds or publicity, not proof. Signed receipts are commoditizing (IETF draft, Signet). It also keeps the full inline gate, and it spreads the 25 calls across insurers, platforms and SMBs, which leaves only 15 agency conversations to test the paying buyer.
scores.best_idea_to_graft: The audit metric 'commitment errors the agency had NOT caught'. It tests the silent-failure thesis (Roark) directly. Also: a €1,500 pilot price floor, which is a stronger willingness-to-pay test than €249-490.

scores.name: Kept (a snuepi rework): independent booking-truth verification and client proof reports for voice-AI agencies (lens contrarian)
scores.fatal_flaw: The retention premise is vendor-sourced. The claims that 70-80% of churn is perception and that a dashboard reduces cancellations come from Trillet and MyVoiceAIConnect, which sell those dashboards. No agency has said it would pay for a proof report. Post-call reconciliation is also easy to copy (Cekura, Roark or the platforms could add it), and it needs read-only API and calendar access, which may stop agencies from trying it at all.
scores.best_idea_to_graft: Observe first, gate later. A post-call reconciliation audit on real call logs measures the actual production error rate before anything is built. The inline gate only ships in v1.5, and only if pilots ask for it after seeing their own numbers.

judgements.winner: Kept (a snuepi rework): independent booking-truth verification and client proof reports for voice-AI agencies (lens contrarian)
judgements.rationale: Counting only what the evidence supports, all four designs share the same demand base. Builder-level pain is heavily documented: false 'booked', wrong dates and timezones, double-booking and invented prices on Vapi, Retell and n8n. Agency willingness to pay is only inferred, from Cekura's $500/mo plan and agency retainers. No first-person case shows an agency losing a client or paying for a runtime guard. Demand and willingness to pay therefore score the same across designs (3 and 2). The real difference is how each design treats the counter-evidence. Builders hand-roll token gates, platforms keep absorbing the date and duplicate slices, and GHL claims native double-booking prevention. Every one of those signals weakens an inline gate as the first product, and D1, D2 and D3 all lead with one. Kept (D4) is the only design that follows from the counter-evidence. It goes after failures that are silent and only visible against ground truth (Roark's 'passes as success until the patient complains'). It sits off the call path, so it adds no latency or liability. Its first sale is an audit on real logs that measures production error rates, the number every design admits it lacks. It is also the most realistic for one founder: an extraction and reconciliation pipeline on top of existing connectors, time logic and reply-guard patterns, with no adapters on four platforms that sit in the call path. Caveats: its churn and dashboard premise is vendor marketing, its moat is speed and channel, and log-access friction could kill it (kill criterion 2 tests this). Grafts for the winner: D1's no-access stress test as the opener before the audit. D3's 'errors the agency had not caught' metric and a higher pilot price floor (about €1,000-1,500 rather than €249), to get a real willingness-to-pay signal. D2's explicit platform-absorption kill trigger and its fresh free/busy check, both for the v1.5 gate. Park the insurer and ledger story (D3) until an insurer or managing general agent states demand. Today it is speculation, not evidence.
